entry.title: Re: ROMs that copy themselves to SRAM? (ADFS E00?)
entry.content:
Steve Picton (who runs IFEL) has just sent me an SSD image that contains some bootloaders he wrote a few ago:
The attached SSD is a boot loader for ADFS 1.31, an 8271 DFS and ACP DFS for 1770 (all Model B). They work slightly differently to others in that there is no auto-RAM detection. The target RAM socket must be specified by the very first byte of the ROM. Eg with RAM in socket 7

*LOAD ADFSBL 2000
?&2000 = 7
*SAVE ADFSBL 2000+4000

A real POR (or simulated with ?&FE4E=127) is required.

You can freely upload this to Stardot.
Here's the SSD containing these:
BtLoader 1.ssd
This works quite nicely, and gives the user explicit control over which sideways RAM slot is used:
cap1.png

Dave
Oooh thank you both, will give this a whirl.

Though I have started to think of some customizations I want to make that my own ROM enables. For example, in my case, the USB4VC device that I used to connect my keyboard, does not support the dip config on the keyboard. So I presently have to manually set the floppy drive access speed to its fastest setting. Will share where I land back here. Meanwhile thanks so much!

Which is not quite on page boundary (as it looks like MMFS uses) so the compare/copy code will need a tweak. Also it does appear to change 8001 (or 0001) for some reason. I do not require any credit, but want to acknowledge the original author for sure.

Currently has "(C) Based on work by Coeus"
The original idea was mine and I came up with an initial implementation (I am Steve Fosdick in the (C) in MMFS bootstrap), but Dave (Hoglet) has significantly enhanced it by making it more reliable, able to work on an Electron, and faster so I think he should also receive credit. The Martin Mather credit in the MMFS bootstrap (C) is for the MMFS payload: MMFS was originally written by Martin though more recently maintained by Hoglet.
Hello, Coeus! First of all thank you very much for this brilliant idea. Secondly, thanks for the info on the acknowledgements. I'll work through some more testing and get things ready for further review on this thread. Thanks all!

entry.title: Re: ROMs that copy themselves to SRAM? (ADFS E00?)
entry.content:
Actually when I press soft-break I get ...

'RAM/ROM comparison failed at'

I assume other some magic value needs changing in the code... will. keep looking.
I guess you must already have updated the two-byte MAGIC number so it was correct for ADFS?
SYSVARS.asm:

Code: 

MAGIC0=&19
MAGIC1=&67
boostrap.asm:

Code: 

;; Step 2: Test if that pre-existing rom image is SWMMFS
;; so we re-use the same slot again and again
        lda     &b5fe
        cmp     #MAGIC0
        bne     romnxt
        lda     &b5ff
        cmp     #MAGIC1
        bne     romnxt
This is used so the bootstrap ROM can quickly identify the existing ROM as ADFS. You need to pick a couple of locations in ADFS to use for this. It doesn't have to be bf5e/b5ff, it can be anywhere in the ROM.

The other reasons for this error are:

1. You are including part of the workspace at the end of the ROM in the data being copied. When this changes, you will get this error. You need to exclude the workspace at the end.

2. E00 ADFS is writing to itself in a part of the ROM that is still covered by the check. Either because it's using self-modifying code, or becase it's storing data intermixed with code.

Dave
Thanks yes, I changed the two magic values, otherwise it was replicating itself into my other sram's

I will review the other reason you have listed - most useful - thx!
